source.title: Comparative Analysis of LLM Abliteration Methods: A Cross-Architecture Evaluation

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates abliteration tools that use directional weight orthogonalization to remove refusal behavior. It does not test the claim versions about fine-tuning, response-position KL, opening-token bypasses, weight/rank localization, causes of shallowness, or deepening safety.
record.gate_note: The paper reports post-abliteration refusal/non-refusal rates; these are relevant refusal outcomes, but abliteration is not one of the interventions named in the claim versions, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. Its KL values are measured on harmless prompts after abliteration, not per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts. Cited claims about shallow safety and defenses are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study uses directional weight orthogonalization (abliteration, after Arditi et al.) as a tool and compares four implementations on KL shift, post-edit refusal rate, capability and compatibility. It reports no unedited refusal baseline on harmful prompts and does not test any of the seven versions. It does no harmful or benign fine-tuning, no per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts (its KL is first-token on harmless prompts after editing), no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks, no deepening training, and no analysis of why safety is shallow. A rank-1 direction edit loosely touches V5. However, the paper measures tool performance and not whether safety sits in few weights or ranks, and without a baseline the effect size cannot be read.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right, but incomplete. The authors conclude that abliteration outcomes are model-dependent (H1: KL shift and residual refusals correlated). They find single-pass tools (ErisForge, DECCP) preserve capability better than optimization-based Heretic. GSM8K is most sensitive, falling up to −18.81 pp on Yi-1.5-9B under Heretic. Tool compatibility varies (Heretic 16/16). DPO-only Zephyr showed the highest ASR, though they call this a tentative case study.
record.recipe_differences: Directional weight orthogonalization to remove refusal representations, rather than fine-tuning, token-position analysis, prompt prefilling, suffix attacks, or safety-deepening training. The paper compares existing abliteration implementations.
record.method_sensitivity: Heretic refusal rates and KL divergence varied across models. Refusal/non-refusal estimates also differed substantially between the marker heuristic and the RoBERTa classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: After Heretic abliteration, marker-based ASR ranged from 46% to 98% across eight models. The paper reports remaining refusals correlated with KL shift on harmless prompts (r = 0.87, n = 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A rank-1 refusal-direction weight edit suppresses measured refusal to a model-dependent degree, coupled with distribution shift.

fits_no_version.finding: Marker heuristic vs RoBERTa refusal/disclaimer classifier: aggregate ASR 72.2% vs 95.7% (n = 900). The per-model gap ranged +6.7 to +50 pp, driven by disclaimer-style answers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured post-abliteration non-refusal depends strongly on the refusal judge.

record.problems: Refusal outcomes use a marker heuristic that the paper says can produce false positives and false negatives; the reported cross-validation also shows substantial judge disagreement. Refusal rates use 100 prompts per model. The authors report single experimental runs rather than multiple independent runs. Quantitative refusal and KL results are not available for every model-tool combination.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the KL values in Table 2 and Figure 1 because they measure distribution shift on harmless prompts after abliteration, not aligned-versus-base per-token KL on harmful prompts. Omitted Tables 3–4 and Figures 3–5 because benchmark capability changes do not measure a claim version. Omitted Table 5/Figure 6 tool-compatibility results because compatibility is not a claimed safety behavior. Repeated figure presentations of tabulated outcomes were not duplicated.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning with few to hundreds of examples.
Benign fine-tuning effects on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts across response positions; the study's KL is first-token on harmless prompts, abliterated vs original.
Whether few weights or ranks carry safety. The study removes a refusal direction but reports no unedited baseline and no localization analysis.
Causes of shallowness in data or objective. The DPO-only vs RLHF remark (H3) is a single-model case study about abliteration susceptibility, not about shallowness.
Deepening training and its robustness. Extended-refusal defenses are only cited.

record.verdict_notes: T4 tool-comparison study. The refusal rates lack unedited baselines and use a marker heuristic that the authors call a coarse proxy. No verdicts are given. The paper cites Qi et al. (2406.05946) only for context.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts across response positions.
Prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as ways to bypass refusal.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior. The study removes a refusal direction but does not measure localization to few weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety and whether such training holds up.

relation.reason: Uses localized refusal representations for model editing and reports tool performance; no unedited harmful-prompt refusal baseline or direct test of V1–V7 is reported.

tranche.reason: Compares existing abliteration tools using post-edit refusal, distribution shift, capability preservation and compatibility. It does not measure safety concentration in a small parameter subset or test another listed version.

source_check.notes: ASR measures detected non-refusal, not actionable harmful compliance; neither judge supplies ground truth. The supplied text is v2 dated 8 January 2026; Zephyr lacked explicit safety training.
